newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegoil stocks seen rising due to strike.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegoil stocks seen rising due to strike.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil stocks are likely to rise as supplies to mills from storage tanks at ports have been halted by a road tanker strike, dealers said on Saturday.
Stocks rose to 194,500 tonnes by Friday from 136,000 tonnes on December 21, and at least 70,850 tonnes of more oil was expected to reach Karachi by January 10, one dealer said.
Despite the strike, prices of imported vegetable oils have not fluctuated much as mills had already bought domestic cottonseed oil, he said.
Existing stocks include 165,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil, 16,000 tonnes of soyoil and sunflower oil and 13,500 tonnes of palm olein, the dealer said.
The state-run Ghee Corp of Pakistan has also booked 6,000 tonnes of palm oil for shipment by January 31, the dealer said.

Indicative prices in the local market for RBD palm oil rose to $555 per tonne C&F for January shipment from $552.50 last week. Soyoil closed unchanged at $557.50 and palm fatty acid distillates closed steady at $335, the dealer said.

In Pakistani rupees, the rate for palm oil at Keamari port fell to 1,218 per maund (37.32 kg) from 1,225 last week and soyoil closed unchanged at 1,230. Cottonseed oil rose to 1,175 rupees per maund from 1,160 last week, the dealer said.
Pakistan Vanaspati Manufacturers Association president Tanveer Hassan said the strike was likely to end in a few days as tanker operators were continuing negotiations with the strikers.
